shows: Every request on a signed route that named the room and reached it through the front before the last receipt was signed is in this list, in the order it ran, and none was still running.
does_not_show: Reads leave no receipt. A plain heartbeat sent just before the room was marked serial leaves none.
A bulk delete, the reaper and an API restart can remove the room without a receipt. A last action that is a successful exec, file put or file get shows the room was alive when it ran.
Programs left running inside the room: its main process, a program an earlier exec left behind, a process started by process_start.
A front restart loses the serial mark and the key; a run that spans one fails.

checked: run mode: checks 1 to 8 of the one-shot file

run.context_check: the signed context file and the request in the file
shows: A machine with this measurement started this image, with nothing added at create.
These input files and this context were written. This command ran with this environment on top of the image's own.

These output files were then read, and the room was still there after the last read. Between its start and the end marker, no other request that can run something in the room, write to it or change its limit reached it through the machine's front.
does_not_show: That a second run gives the same output.
The exit code, unless the exec answer in the file hashes to the signed result (see exit_code).
That the room is gone: the delete is clean-up.
Which build the measurement stands for: it is checked against the measurements you allowed.
The request headers of file calls: they are in neither the signed target nor any hash.
Reads (logs, for one): they leave no receipt.
That the machine's disk was left unaltered by its host: the receipts do not show it either way.
That the approved build is the same as the published source: the allowed measurements are your own list.
